correctness.rationale: For the 48 unrescaled roots the coordinate inequalities show VR_1 is the stellar subdivision of all octahedral facets of the convex 24-cell boundary, hence S3. Reconstructed standalone files verify the exact squared-distance spectrum, face vectors (48,240,384,192) and (48,408,1224,1560,840,168,24), and recheck every 1704-pair deletion: each lower face has exactly one surviving immediate coface and the final complex is exactly VR_1. Thus VR_sqrt2 simplicially collapses to VR_1 and the inclusion induces integral homology isomorphisms. The W(F4) determinant action follows from the equivariant 24-cell geometric realization, not from a claim that the collapse is equivariant.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge original contribution is the exact inclusion-preserving 1704-pair collapse at the second Euclidean distance scale for the full 48-point F4 roots, hence an integral homotopy-equivalence statement and an orientation-compatible degree-three persistence interval. The radius-one stellar subdivision and ordinary 24-cell topology are standard consequences and explicitly credited; they are not advanced as novel. Actual semantic searches in published-finding corpus, the related published mathematical-claim records, and targeted primary literature yielded no implication covering this collapse. Residual unindexed/alternate-name coverage is possible.

value.rationale: The full 48-root F4 configuration is a canonical exceptional crystallographic point set. Its second Euclidean distance jump inserts 3408 simplices and raises simplicial dimension from three to six, yet an explicit integral collapse preserves a fundamental S3 class and its Weyl orientation representation. This inclusion-preserving result is a precise motivated persistence benchmark beyond the standard 24-cell boundary fact and beyond numerical Betti tables; no higher-scale or general-root-family theorem is asserted.
